extraction.name: AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes
extraction.description: AMASS is a large and varied database of human motion that unifies 15 different optical marker-based mocap datasets by representing them within a common framework and parameterization. It uses a new method, MoSh++, that converts mocap data into realistic 3D human meshes represented by a rigged body model (SMPL). The consistent representation of AMASS makes it readily useful for animation, visualization, and generating training data for deep learning. The dataset contains more than 40 hours of motion data, spanning over 300 subjects, and more than 11000 motions.
extraction.creator: Naureen Mahmood, Nima Ghorbani, Nikolaus F. Troje, Gerard Pons-Moll, Michael J. Black
extraction.citeAs: Naureen Mahmood, Nima Ghorbani, Nikolaus F. Troje, Gerard Pons-Moll, Michael J. Black. AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes. arXiv:1904.03278, 2019.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The AMASS dataset was created by unifying 15 existing optical marker-based motion capture datasets. A new method called MoSh++ was developed to convert the raw mocap data into realistic 3D human meshes represented by the SMPL body model, including SMPL 3D shape parameters (16 dimensions), DMPL soft tissue coefficients (8 dimensions), and full SMPL pose parameters (90 dimensions) with hand articulations. Some datasets were downloaded from the internet, while others (Dancers, Transitions, BioMotionLab, and SSM) were obtained privately or recorded by the authors. The SSM dataset was specifically collected using an OptiTrack mocap system with 67 markers synchronized with a 3dMD 4D body scanning system to provide ground truth 3D data for hyperparameter tuning and evaluation of MoSh++.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Physical data collection, Software Collection, Experiments
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: During mocap sessions, markers may get occluded by the body due to pose. If multiple markers of a particular body part are occluded simultaneously, the optimization may result in unreliable and implausible poses. Additionally, due to inherent problems with mocap, such as swapped and mislabeled markers, the results were manually inspected and problems were either corrected or held out.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The dataset is built upon 15 existing optical marker-based motion capture datasets, including ACCAD, BioMotion Lab, CMU, EKUT, Eyes Japan, HumanEva, KIT, MPI HDM05, MPI Limits, MPI MoSh, SFU, SSM, TCD Hand, TotalCapture, and Transitions. These source datasets contain varying markersets ranging in size from 37 to 91 markers. The SSM dataset was collected using an OptiTrack motion capture system with 67 reflective mocap markers and a 3dMD 4D body scanning system.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: In cases where there are no markers present on the hands of the recorded subjects, the hand poses are set to the average pose of the MANO model. To address issues with occluded markers leading to implausible poses, a coefficient 'q' was introduced to vary the pose prior weight as a factor of the number of missing markers. The more markers missing, the higher this weights the pose prior.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The core manipulation involves converting raw marker data into SMPL body model parameters using the MoSh++ method. This process fits the surface of the SMPL/DMPL body model to observed mocap markers, recovering soft-tissue dynamics and realistic hand motion. Each frame in AMASS includes 16-dimension SMPL 3D shape parameters, 8-dimension DMPL soft tissue coefficients, and 90-dimension full SMPL pose parameters, including hand articulations.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The source datasets, which contained varying markersets (37 to 91 markers), were unified into a single format using MoSh++. This involved standardizing the representation to SMPL pose, shape, and soft-tissue parameters. Manual inspection was performed to correct or hold out problems arising from swapped and mislabeled markers in the raw mocap data.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The 'annotations' in AMASS are the derived SMPL body model parameters (shape, pose, and soft-tissue dynamics). These were generated by the MoSh++ method, which fits the SMPL/DMPL body model to sparse motion capture markers. The process involves two stages: Stage I optimizes poses, a single shape, and latent marker positions, excluding soft-tissue deformations. Stage II optimizes pose for each frame, including soft-tissue deformation coefficients. Hyperparameters for the objective functions were tuned using cross-validation on the Synchronized Scans and Markers (SSM) dataset, minimizing the distance between ground truth 3D scans and estimated 3D body meshes.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The accuracy of MoSh++ was evaluated using scan-to-model distances between ground truth 3D scans from the SSM dataset and the corresponding estimated meshes. For each reconstructed mocap frame, a uniform sampling of 10,000 points from the 3D scan was used to compute the distance to the closest surface point in the reconstructed mesh, and the average of these distances (in mm) was measured. Hyperparameters were tuned to minimize this reconstruction error on validation data. The optimal number of shape (16) and dynamic (8) coefficients was determined by minimizing error on a held-out validation set, noting that more components could lead to overfitting.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: MoSh++, SMPL body model, DMPL, MANO hand model, Chumpy
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The AMASS dataset is publicly available to the research community at http://amass.is.tue.mpg.de. The maintainers plan to continuously expand the dataset by adding more data, and will support the community in contributing new captures as long as they can be similarly shared.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains human motion data, including 3D body shape, pose, and soft-tissue deformations for 346 subjects. For the SSM dataset, two of the three subjects were professional models who signed modeling contracts, allowing their 4D scan data and synchronized mocap data to be released.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Current runtime for MoSh++ is not real-time. Allowing too many shape or dynamic components can lead to overfitting to mocap markers, causing higher error compared with ground truth shape. The dataset does not currently include captures with articulated facial mocap markers. The velocity constancy weights (u and v) were empirically determined and could not be optimized using just one source of data, as they depend on mocap system calibration, tracking quality, frame rate, and motion types.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning for deep learning models of human motion. Animation, visualization, and generating synthetic training data for computer vision tasks. The dataset is intended for the research community.
